references.text: The original instruction to make five pillars with gold-plated hooks and five bases of bronze for the curtain at the entrance of the tent.
Describes the pillars with silver hooks and bases of bronze in the construction of the courtyard, showing the recurring pattern of metalwork in the tabernacle.
Parallel description of pillars with hooks and bases of bronze in the courtyard, part of the same building account.
Further details about the pillars' bases of bronze and hooks of silver, showing the consistent design in the structure of the tabernacle.
Describes four pillars with bases of bronze and hooks of gold, a similar construction to that in verse 38.
Refers to the collection of bronze as a gift offering, the material used for the bases mentioned in this verse.
The reference illustrates how the same material principles (bronze base/silver hook) are consistently repeated throughout the surroundings of the tabernacle.
This is a direct fulfillment reference where the actual execution (36:38) confirms obedience to the original divine instruction (27:10).
Confirms that the same symbolic materials (bronze/silver) are used consistently on all sides of the tabernacle's courtyard.
Illustrates the consistency in God's plan by showing that even the smaller sides (10 pillars) follow the same material principles as the entrance.
Connects the concrete execution of the pillars in 36:38 directly to the source of the material (the people's silver gift), emphasizing the theology of voluntary offering.
